answer: A bond is refunded only after 13 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. The vertex counter is kept in ledge and canyon publishes each reset. A hostile operator therefore has to keep every alias continuously active for 13 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 11 times over for the same share of the pool. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
